corrections.claim: King points pick their option through D.pick (D.java:203-209).
corrections.correction: King points pick through DK.netPick, which wraps the same DNet.sample: a masked softmax plus floor/m on each allowed option. The sampling semantics in the report are right, but the cited path is not.
corrections.evidence: DK.java:358-365 (netPick), used at DK.java:495 and 620; DNet.java:116-135.

corrections.claim: A_BITE with no target: the attack throws, and the exception is caught at DK.java:499.
corrections.correction: Nothing is thrown. King.weakest(enemies) returns null, so execKingAct returns false and zdb's own bite runs as the fallback (unless coop or hold skips it).
corrections.evidence: DK.java:507-509 (b == null -> return false); King.java:57 (zdb bite skipped when coop or hold).

corrections.claim: A_BITE_KING falls back because the king cannot act ('in the data, always').
corrections.correction: It always falls back, but for a geometric reason, not a data one. The executor needs rc.canAttack(enemy king's centre). A king can only attack within dist^2 8 of its own centre. Two 3x3 kings cannot overlap, so their centres are at least Chebyshev 3 apart (dist^2 >= 9), and the option can never execute. The same centre test makes the KING_ACT feature kingReach always false, and it leaves enemy kings out of the reach/weak/kill-bite features. zdb's own bite does hit king body tiles, so the features and the actual targets disagree.
corrections.evidence: DK.java:551-553 (A_BITE_KING executor); GameConstants.java:179 (RAT_KING_ATTACK_DISTANCE_SQUARED = 8); RobotControllerImpl.java:1046-1052; DK.java:241-255 (reach/weak/kingReach from canAttack(e.location)); King.java:205-225 (weakest/kingTile body tiles); DK.java:579-589 (weakestLoc).

corrections.claim: KING_ACT's trap/dirt/dig cooldowns close KING_SPAWN on the next turn; fort traps and moat fill put the king on cooldown for 1-2 turns.
corrections.correction: Cooldown drops by 10 each turn, and the king is ready only when cooldown < 10, so the leftover cooldown when it acts is 0 or 5. Attacks and cat traps (cost 10) never block the next turn. A rat trap (15) blocks the next turn only if 5 was left over, so it blocks 0 or 1 turns. Dirt place/remove and digs (25) block 1 or 2 turns. Only the 25-cost actions reliably close the next turn's KING_SPAWN. Within one turn the coupling runs the other way: a build (cost 10) leaves the king not ready, so KING_ACT never opens after a build.
corrections.evidence: InternalRobot.java:354-355 (ready iff < COOLDOWN_LIMIT), 1167 (-10 per turn); GameConstants.java:244, 257; RobotControllerImpl.java:1016 (build cooldown).

corrections.claim: Traps placed on ring tiles make those tiles unbuildable (a spawn/act coupling).
corrections.correction: canBuildRat checks only range, action-ready, cheese, occupancy and passability. isPassable is false only for walls, dirt and flying robots. Traps do not block builds; dirt (moat fill) and occupancy do. The report's missing_information says it did not check this.

corrections.claim: A_CAT_TRAP is allowed only in cooperation or within 100 rounds of a backstab.
corrections.correction: The engine rule is coop OR (at most 100 rounds since the backstab AND our team is not the backstabber). The engine also caps cat traps at 10 per team, a cap shared with babies, who lay cat traps too. A cat trap also needs its cheese cost and a passable, unoccupied tile with no own trap and no mine. The 19.8% coop fallback probably includes hits on the team cap.
corrections.evidence: GameWorld.java:420-423 (catTrapsAllowed); TrapType.java:17 (maxCount 10); RobotControllerImpl.java:339-364, 356; Baby.java:823, 851 (babies place cat traps).

corrections.claim: KING_SPAWN options fall back only on engine preconditions.
corrections.correction: S_DIG can also fail on the bot's own guard: digRing returns without digging when the bank is below 45. That is policy, not an engine rule. The proposal's masks need this predicate too.

corrections.claim: A newborn baby's role comes from Baby.born.
corrections.correction: In net builds, BABY_ROLE (point 5) is sampled at birth right after born(), and roleExec(k) overrides the role born() set. The recorded label is the final role.
corrections.evidence: Baby.java:41-46 (born(); D.pick(D.BABY_ROLE, D.roleOk(0)); roleExec(k); D.lab = D.roleLab()).

corrections.claim: A king forms only when babies fill the 3x3.
corrections.correction: becomeRatKing needs at least 7 allied baby rats among the 9 tiles. All 9 tiles must be on the map and passable, with no cat or king in the 3x3. The team also needs cheese >= 50, fewer than 5 kings, and fewer than 2 kings after round 1200.
corrections.evidence: RobotControllerImpl.java:1158-1213 (numAllyRats < 7 throws at ~1211); GameConstants.java:68 (5 kings), 75 (2 after cutoff), 82 (cutoff 1200), 219 (upgrade cost 50).

corrections.claim: A_BITE_KILL: a cheese-boosted kill bite on the weakest enemy (fallback explained only by targets/bank).
corrections.correction: biteCheese returns 0, and the option falls back, when the target has hp <= 10 (a plain bite already kills it) or when (hp-10)^2 > min(100, bank-300). So A_BITE_KILL executes only on targets with 11-20 hp and a bank of at least 300 + (hp-10)^2. Its mask should be biteCheese > 0 && canAttack(loc, c), which DK.java:253 already computes as a feature (that feature excludes kings).

corrections.claim: Records go out as indicator strings capped at 256 chars (GameConstants.java:53; truncation at RobotControllerImpl.java:1579-1581). Per-candidate KING_ACT records (~190 chars) still fit; only a merged record would reach the limit.
corrections.correction: In recorded runs the 256 cap does not apply. The student harness intercepts '\uDEC0' strings at the top of setIndicatorString, before the engine truncates, and Decisions.take writes all n features. The real limit is the bot's buffer: D.F/F2 = char[192]. That buffer holds the 4 header chars, the features and the RL trailer (5 + ceil(nOpt/16) chars). The trailer is silently dropped when it would not fit, and D.f has no bounds check. A ~190-char KING_ACT record already overflows today's buffer. Raising it is a one-line change, but the cost estimate should plan around 192, not 256.
corrections.evidence: D.java:112 (char[192]); D.java:140-142 (trailer dropped if at+5+words > B.length); D.java:164-167 (F[n++] unchecked); D.java:179; scripts/build_student.py:52-55; java/student/alpha0/student/Decisions.java:32-49.

corrections.claim: KING_FORM options 0-6 are the same action with a site open, and 0-2 equal 8-12 with no site open.
corrections.correction: With a site open, options 0-3, 5 and 6 just close it. F_RICH_GAP (4) also sets formStart = round - FORM_TTL - FORM_RETRY, which reopens zdb's own formation gate at once, so its effect is different. With no site open, 0-2 still call closeForm and write FORM_T = 0, while 8-12 write nothing. They are the same only when FORM_T is already 0.

missed: KING_MOVE also uses the king's action. K_DIG, K_DIGSTEP_N and K_DODGE dig after KING_ACT has run (King.java:395-400, 445-455; DK.java:412-417, 430-433). A merged 'one king-action decision per action-ready turn' still leaves this second consumer of the action outside it.

Rat traps placed in cooperation (A_TRAP_FORT/A_TRAP_FOE/A_TRAP_*) carry a backstab risk. When an enemy triggers our rat trap, the engine calls backstab against the trigger's opponent (GameWorld.java:639-642). That ends coop, makes OUR team the backstabber, and with it removes our cat-trap rights (GameWorld.java:420-423). The trap executors never check G.coop (DK.java:520-562, 602-616). Bites and grabs on rats also backstab (InternalRobot.java:623-625, 649); the report covered bites only.

Floor asymmetry at KING_FORM with a site open: 7 of the 8 allowed options close the site. Options 0-2, 5 and 6 call formClose, and 3 and 4 call closeForm (King.java:735-743); only F_HOLD keeps it. At cpi-x0's floor of 0.1, the floor alone closes an open site with probability >= 8.75% per turn, an expected life of at most ~11 turns. This mirrors the 17/25 opener share when no site is open (configs/cpi-x0.json; DK.java:631-640).

Every net open resets King.formStart = round (King.java:714). zdb's formation gate (King.java:698: round - formStart < FORM_TTL 60 + FORM_RETRY 150 -> F_IDLE) and endKing (King.java:~765) both read formStart. So each exploratory open shuts zdb's own formation off for up to 210 rounds (Cfg.java:44). This likely explains why the gate rarely passes. F_RICH_GAP does the opposite (King.java:742).

Openers are not masked for the engine's king limits. formAllowed masks them only at numKings >= KING_SLOTS 5 (DK.java:637-638; Comms.java:12). After round 1200, a team with >= 2 kings cannot form another (GameConstants.java:75-82; RobotControllerImpl.java ~1173-1176), yet sites can still open and pull babies. zdb itself caps formation at FORM_MAX 2 (Cfg.java:46; King.java:731), or 4 with a rich bank (Cfg.java:52).

An open formation site affects baby points beyond the report's list: the BABY_MOVE mask M_FORM_KING (Baby.java:2268), the endCat skip while a site is fresh (Baby.java:1411), auto-promotion in the action phase (Baby.java:181-184), and the comms FORM-age feature that every baby point reads (D.java:698).

Answers to the report's open question on team dirt: team dirt starts at 0 (TeamInfo.java:31), gains 1 per removeDirt and loses 1 per placeDirt (TeamInfo.java:223-233). placeDirt needs team dirt > 0 and a tile that is not a mine (RobotControllerImpl.java:253-274). So moat fill depends on earlier digs, by kings or babies.

Engine trap caps the action-space masks need: 25 rat traps per team (TrapType.java:12) and 10 cat traps per team (TrapType.java:17). Babies count toward both caps, and king traps take their cheese from the shared bank.

The KING_ACT feature spawnWhy (DK.java:280) never takes its 'build' value. A build costs cooldown 10, which leaves the king not action-ready, so KING_ACT does not open on that turn. The 'b' value is dead for that point.
overall_reliability: Mostly reliable on data and core structure; less reliable on engine rules and cross-point couplings. Every measured number I checked (kpts-cpi-x0/kpts2/kpts3 outputs, cpi-x0-summary.json, the plan table at docs/rl-es-plan.md:500-506) reproduced. So did the descriptions of masks, executors, fallback mechanics, feature/label lists, and the claim that fallen-back picks still drive the RL gradient (scripts/rl_train.py:525-542; the flags are read only at line 538). Two claims are wrong: A_BITE does not throw, and traps do not block builds. Several are partly wrong or incomplete: cooldown blocking, cat-trap legality, kill-bite conditions, king-formation rules, the newborn's role source, the 256 vs 192 record limit, and which KING_FORM options are equivalent. One mechanism is misexplained: A_BITE_KING is geometrically impossible, and the same flaw blinds the kingReach/reach features to enemy kings. It also missed couplings that matter to its own proposal: KING_MOVE digs share the action, rat traps can trigger a coop backstab, exploratory opens reset formStart, and the floor churns open sites. None of these overturns the main conclusion: fallback comes from masks that do not match executor preconditions, and per-candidate masks plus executors would fix it. Several do change what the masks and features must contain.
proposal_concerns: A merged king-action decision must also include KING_MOVE's digs (K_DIG, K_DIGSTEP_N, K_DODGE), since they use the same action after KING_ACT. Otherwise the 'one record per action-ready turn' design still has two consumers of the king's action.

The proposed 'action-cooldown cost' feature should encode turns blocked, not raw cost. With a leftover of 0 or 5, cost 10 never blocks the next turn, 15 blocks 0-1 turns and 25 blocks 1-2. Only the 25-cost actions (dirt, digs) reliably cost the next turn's spawn.

Masks meant to equal executor preconditions need more than the canPlace* calls. They must cover the engine trap caps (rat 25, cat 10, both shared with babies), exclusion of the backstabber, cheese costs from the shared bank, and attack-tile passability. They also need a coop guard or feature for rat traps (an enemy trigger makes us the backstabber) as well as bites. And they must include the bot-side guard on S_DIG (bank < 45).

Drop A_BITE_KING, or retarget it to enemy-king body tiles as King.kingTile does. Rewrite the kingReach/reach/weak features to test body tiles too. Per-target candidates built on the current canAttack(e.location) logic would inherit the blind spot to enemy kings.

The KING_SPAWN per-tile mask can be exactly canBuildRat(tile). Traps never block builds, so the proposed trap-on-tile features are not needed to explain build failures; dirt and occupancy are what block.

The KING_FORM redesign (commitment/TTL, minimum babies) should also separate net opens from King.formStart. Otherwise zdb's own gate stays off for 210 rounds after each exploratory open. It should also fix the floor asymmetry: 7 of 8 allowed options close an open site, and 17 of 25 open one when none is open. One fix is an open/keep/close head sampled before the site kind. Openers should be masked by the engine's king limits (2 after round 1200), or sites that cannot form will still pull babies.

Size the records against the bot's 192-char D.F buffer, which includes the header and the RL trailer, or raise it. The engine's 256 cap is bypassed in harness runs. At the proposed ~190 chars, a KING_ACT record would already overflow or lose its trailer.
